svg.text: The agentic platform in one picture
One front door, one identity per agent, one gateway out, one register: how agents are admitted, contained and watched.
A tier opens only once the roles it needs are staffed. Humans raise an
agent's autonomy; machines can only lower it.
Tiers: C no-code, read-only · R read tools · W writes · P privileged (the
Workspace super-admin agent, Wall-E) · X general capability, not opened

kill switches: halt in seconds; fleet-wide by
everything registered feeds it; an agent that stops feeding it has its actions halted
Audit logs and telemetry: every action, model call and admin change, stored immutably in the EU (400 days to 10 years by data class); sensitive-data scanning on the
Detections: an outsourced security monitoring desk (people on call, using a SIEM, a security monitoring tool); every finding names an owner and a deadline
The independent controller agent (Eve): watches the agents and the human administrators, reports to a person independent of the agent's owner, can halt an agent's
actions; its evidence is copied daily to a witness outside the tenant
Evaluation: a blind grader scores a sample of each agent's work before and after admission; a falling score lowers its autonomy
A hundredth agent costs a register row, a factory run and a budget line, and inherits controls reviewed once.
Two grades of control, tagged on every box: what Google or code refuses, and what is only detected. A content screen is detection, even when set to block.
A privileged agent costs more than a read-only one: a second person, an outsourced monitoring desk, a witness outside the tenant and a signed deviation.
Status on 2026-09-23: designed, not built. Agent Gateway and Agent Identity for Gemini Enterprise are Preview on that date. Full design: the agentic-platform wiki, 01-hld.md.
